result.summary: 2023 was the year of The Coming Wave book tour, and Suleyman made many dated predictions that year. New ones found here: the Modern Turing Test being 'as little as two years away' (MIT Technology Review, July 2023), parameter-scale predictions in the co-written Foreign Affairs essay, and a 1,000x-larger-models-in-three-years line on 80,000 Hours. The Foreign Affairs essay also has the open-source two-to-three-year claim 13 days before the recorded date, and the full 80,000 Hours, Diary of a CEO and Intelligence Squared transcripts were cut off, so they may hold more.

reply_text:
Now the Diary of a CEO transcript and the Intelligence Squared page.I found three new dated predictions from 2023 that aren't on your list. Two more items match recorded claims. One is an earlier 2023 version of a recorded claim; the other repeats one. The biggest gap is that I couldn't read the full 80,000 Hours and Diary of a CEO transcripts or most of the Intelligence Squared talk, so I may have missed claims there.

**New candidates:**
- **14 July 2023, MIT Technology Review essay (his own byline):** "Something like this could be as little as two years away." "This" is an AI passing his "Modern Turing Test": turning $100,000 into $1 million on a retail web platform within a few months, with humans approving only a few steps.
- **16 August 2023, Foreign Affairs essay written with Ian Bremmer:** models with tens of trillions of parameters "in the next couple of years," and "brain scale" models (over 100 trillion parameters) "within five years." I read this on a third-party copy, not on foreignaffairs.com. Because it's co-written, the words can't be credited to Suleyman alone.
- **1 September 2023, 80,000 Hours podcast:** models "1,000x larger than they currently are in the next three years." This one is borderline. It's about model scale, which is close to the compute forecasts your rules exclude. I left out the next sentence about Inflection's own plans because that's a company plan.

**Matches to recorded claims:**
- **Open-source models (`2023-08-29-suleyman-gpt-4-class-open-source-two-to-three-years.toml`):** the same Foreign Affairs essay already says future models will reach open source "just two or three years" after the big labs build them. That's 13 days before your recorded date.
- **Humanoid robots in 30 years (`2023-09-04-suleyman-humanoid-robotics-next-30-years.toml`):** I found it in a Diary of a CEO transcript on a third-party site. The page is dated March 2024, but the conversation is from 2023. The page doesn't show the air date, so I took 4 September 2023 from your file name.

**Left out:**
- The essay's opening scene ("It's 2035, and artificial intelligence is everywhere") is a hypothetical.
- The MIT Technology Review interview of 15 September has no dated prediction.
- At Intelligence Squared (16 September), "within the next three to five years… human level capability" was the host restating his view, and the page cuts off before his answer.
- The 80,000 Hours "eight, ten, or twelve years" timing for misaligned AI is the host's paraphrase, not his words.

**Pages I couldn't fully read:** The 80,000 Hours page stops just as the "timelines for AI capabilities" section begins. The Diary of a CEO page stops at 28:13, so the "next five years" line a search result placed at 31:45 is unchecked. The Intelligence Squared page stops at about 11 minutes. These are the best places to look next.

I used 9 of 12 searches and all 6 page openings.
